classification.method: fixed host: every load is a new process (cold); no restore exists; warm = the same process's later requests

conclusion: FIXED HOST, NOT LAMBDA. 0xd40 local-file: load 8.085 -> 3.317 s (-4.804 s, 6/6); memfd -4.838 s; warm/forward/RSS no change; answers bit-identical (60/60, 12/12). Same rounds, E9 loads 0.884 s slower than E8 (local, threshold 0.116) and 0.809 s slower (memfd, threshold 0.163), with no other difference: E8 is the better general mechanism. x86_64: the E9 GGUF is refused at load in 6/6 rounds, as designed; the E9 loader with a plain GGUF is inert (answers identical, timings no change). Hazard (October hazard/ files): an UNPATCHED P1 engine loads the E9 GGUF without error and returns NaN probabilities and wrong choices on arm64 and x86_64. A format that silently corrupts answers on any loader without the patch, and needs a KleidiAI build, cannot be a general default. Verdict: general opt-in (arm64 KleidiAI builds with the E9 loader only); prefer E8.

conditions.note: FIXED HOST, NOT LAMBDA LATENCY. One fresh container per load; arms interleaved in reversal-paired random orders (run_ladder.schedule: each arm before its control in exactly half the rounds); page cache primed before round 0; comparisons pair rounds (arm minus p1 in the same round).

cost.note: fixed host already provisioned; no AWS calls

functions.note: memory_mb is P1's Lambda setting, kept for the schema; the container has no memory limit (cgroup memory.max as recorded per load)

hypothesis: A KleidiAI-prepacked GGUF with the E9 loader skips the runtime repack off Lambda too; it must refuse rather than misread on a path without KleidiAI.
reproduce: python3 general/summarize.py <arm64 run> <x86 run> --out <dir> --verdicts general/verdicts.json --commit <analysis sha> --run-id <id>

variance.rule: no change when |median paired delta| <= p1's per-round range or the paired deltas change sign
